newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa still ends up despite NY falls.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa still ends up despite NY falls.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures showed some resilience and maintained modest gains by the close on Wednesday despite profit-taking sales in New York.
Traders said the London market, driven by speculators and funds, was likely to sustain its rise if speculative buying continues.
By the close, September firmed seven stg to 1,117 stg per tonne and front-month July put on eight to 1,099. Technically, the market looks strong if September holds above 1,110 support.
Overall volume, led by active September, was 7,486 lots.

Last week's late rally which continued on Monday was fuelled by what some said were perceptions of tight supplies in the coming crop year and talk harvests being hit by dry weather in late 1997 from the El Nino effect.
Others said supply and weather concerns were probably a little premature.
"What we have seen in the past few days was a strong technical, not fundamental, rally," said one.
On the plus side, one trade house with large long positions was probably the biggest short in the nearby September and December.
"The market may have another go on the upside, but for the time being there could be setbacks," the trader said. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
